transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Thank you very much, Chris.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And thanks to UNLV for hosting us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You know, I think when we talk about the Supreme Court, it really raises the central issue in this election, namely, what kind of country are we going to be?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: What kind of opportunities will we provide for our citizens?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: What kind of rights will Americans have?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I feel strongly that the Supreme Court needs to stand on the side of the American people, not on the side of the powerful corporations and the wealthy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: For me, that means that we need a Supreme Court that will stand up on behalf of women’s rights, on behalf of the rights of the LGBT community, that will stand up and say no to Citizens United, a decision that has undermined the election system in our country because of the way it permits dark, unaccountable money to come into our electoral system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have major disagreements with my opponent about these issues and others that will be before the Supreme Court.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I feel that at this point in our country’s history, it is important that we not reverse marriage equality, that we not reverse Roe v.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Wade, that we stand up against Citizens United, we stand up for the rights of people in the workplace, that we stand up and basically say: The Supreme Court should represent all of us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s how I see the court, and the kind of people that I would be looking to nominate to the court would be in the great tradition of standing up to the powerful, standing up on behalf of our rights as Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I look forward to having that opportunity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I would hope that the Senate would do its job and confirm the nominee that President Obama has sent to them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s the way the Constitution fundamentally should operate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The president nominates, and then the Senate advises and consents, or not, but they go forward with the process.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all, it’s great to be with you, and thank you, everybody.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: The Supreme Court: It’s what it’s all about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Our country is so, so—it’s just so imperative that we have the right justices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Something happened recently where Justice Ginsburg made some very, very inappropriate statements toward me and toward a tremendous number of people, many, many millions of people that I represent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And she was forced to apologize.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And apologize she did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But these were statements that should never, ever have been made.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We need a Supreme Court that in my opinion is going to uphold the Second Amendment, and all amendments, but the Second Amendment, which is under absolute siege.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I believe if my opponent should win this race, which I truly don’t think will happen, we will have a Second Amendment which will be a very, very small replica of what it is right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But I feel that it’s absolutely important that we uphold, because of the fact that it is under such trauma.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I feel that the justices that I am going to appoint—and I’ve named 20 of them—the justices that I’m going to appoint will be pro-life.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They will have a conservative bent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They will be protecting the Second Amendment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They are great scholars in all cases, and they’re people of tremendous respect.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They will interpret the Constitution the way the founders wanted it interpreted.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I believe that’s very, very important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think we should have justices appointed that decide what they want to hear.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s all about the Constitution of—of—and so important, the Constitution the way it was meant to be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And those are the people that I will appoint.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all, I support the Second Amendment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I lived in Arkansas for 18 wonderful years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I represented upstate New York.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I understand and respect the tradition of gun ownership.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It goes back to the founding of our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I also believe that there can be and must be reasonable regulation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Because I support the Second Amendment doesn’t mean that I want people who shouldn’t have guns to be able to threaten you, kill you or members of your family.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And so when I think about what we need to do, we have 33,000 people a year who die from guns.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think we need comprehensive background checks, need to close the online loophole, close the gun show loophole.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There’s other matters that I think are sensible that are the kind of reforms that would make a difference that are not in any way conflicting with the Second Amendment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You mentioned the Heller decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And what I was saying that you referenced, Chris, was that I disagreed with the way the court applied the Second Amendment in that case, because what the District of Columbia was trying to do was to protect toddlers from guns and so they wanted people with guns to safely store them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And the court didn’t accept that reasonable regulation, but they’ve accepted many others.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I see no conflict between saving people’s lives and defending the Second Amendment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, the D.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: vs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Heller decision was very strongly—and she was extremely angry about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I watched.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I mean, she was very, very angry when upheld.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And Justice Scalia was so involved.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And it was a well-crafted decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But Hillary was extremely upset, extremely angry.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And people that believe in the Second Amendment and believe in it very strongly were very upset with what she had to say.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, I was upset because, unfortunately, dozens of toddlers injure themselves, even kill people with guns, because, unfortunately, not everyone who has loaded guns in their homes takes appropriate precautions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But there’s no doubt that I respect the Second Amendment, that I also believe there’s an individual right to bear arms.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That is not in conflict with sensible, commonsense regulation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And, you know, look, I understand that Donald’s been strongly supported by the NRA.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The gun lobby’s on his side.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They’re running millions of dollars of ads against me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I regret that, because what I would like to see is for people to come together and say: of course we’re going to protect and defend the Second Amendment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But we’re going to do it in a way that tries to save some of these 33,000 lives that we lose every year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, let me just tell you before we go any further.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: In Chicago, which has the toughest gun laws in the United States, probably you could say by far, they have more gun violence than any other city.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So we have the toughest laws, and you have tremendous gun violence.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I am a very strong supporter of the Second Amendment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I am—I don’t know if Hillary was saying it in a sarcastic manner, but I’m very proud to have the endorsement of the NRA.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And it’s the earliest endorsement they’ve ever given to anybody who ran for president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So I’m very honored by all of that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We are going to appoint justices—this is the best way to help the Second Amendment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We are going to appoint justices that will feel very strongly about the Second Amendment, that will not do damage to the Second Amendment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, if that would happen, because I am pro-life, and I will be appointing pro-life judges, I would think that that will go back to the individual states.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: If they overturned it, it will go back to the states.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, if we put another two or perhaps three justices on, that’s really what’s going to be—that will happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And that’ll happen automatically, in my opinion, because I am putting pro-life justices on the court.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I will say this: It will go back to the states, and the states will then make a determination.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, I strongly support Roe v.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Wade, which guarantees a constitutional right to a woman to make the most intimate, most difficult, in many cases, decisions about her health care that one can imagine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And in this case, it’s not only about Roe v.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Wade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It is about what’s happening right now in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So many states are putting very stringent regulations on women that block them from exercising that choice to the extent that they are defunding Planned Parenthood, which, of course, provides all kinds of cancer screenings and other benefits for women in our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Donald has said he’s in favor of defunding Planned Parenthood.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He even supported shutting the government down to defund Planned Parenthood.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I will defend Planned Parenthood.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I will defend Roe v.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Wade, and I will defend women’s rights to make their own health care decisions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we have come too far to have that turned back now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And, indeed, he said women should be punished, that there should be some form of punishment for women who obtain abortions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I could just not be more opposed to that kind of thinking.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Because Roe v.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Wade very clearly sets out that there can be regulations on abortion so long as the life and the health of the mother are taken into account.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And when I voted as a senator, I did not think that that was the case.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The kinds of cases that fall at the end of pregnancy are often the most heartbreaking, painful decisions for families to make.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have met with women who toward the end of their pregnancy get the worst news one could get, that their health is in jeopardy if they continue to carry to term or that something terrible has happened or just been discovered about the pregnancy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I do not think the United States government should be stepping in and making those most personal of decisions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So you can regulate if you are doing so with the life and the health of the mother taken into account.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think it’s terrible.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: If you go with what Hillary is saying, in the ninth month, you can take the baby and rip the baby out of the womb of the mother just prior to the birth of the baby.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Now, you can say that that’s OK and Hillary can say that that’s OK.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But it’s not OK with me, because based on what she’s saying, and based on where she’s going, and where she’s been, you can take the baby and rip the baby out of the womb in the ninth month on the final day.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And that’s not acceptable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, that is not what happens in these cases.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And using that kind of scare rhetoric is just terribly unfortunate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You should meet with some of the women that I have met with, women I have known over the course of my life.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This is one of the worst possible choices that any woman and her family has to make.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I do not believe the government should be making it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You know, I’ve had the great honor of traveling across the world on behalf of our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been to countries where governments either forced women to have abortions, like they used to do in China, or forced women to bear children, like they used to do in Romania.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I can tell you: The government has no business in the decisions that women make with their families in accordance with their faith, with medical advice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I will stand up for that right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And, honestly, nobody has business doing what I just said, doing that, as late as one or two or three or four days prior to birth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Nobody has that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all, she wants to give amnesty, which is a disaster and very unfair to all of the people that are waiting in line for many, many years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We need strong borders.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: In the audience tonight, we have four mothers of—I mean, these are unbelievable people that I’ve gotten to know over a period of years whose children have been killed, brutally killed by people that came into the country illegally.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You have thousands of mothers and fathers and relatives all over the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They’re coming in illegally.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Drugs are pouring in through the border.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have no country if we have no border.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Hillary wants to give amnesty.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: She wants to have open borders.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: The border—as you know, the Border Patrol agents, 16,500-plus ICE last week, endorsed me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: First time they’ve ever endorsed a candidate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It means their job is tougher.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But they know what’s going on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They know it better than anybody.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They want strong borders.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They feel we have to have strong borders.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I was up in New Hampshire the other day.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: The biggest complaint they have—it’s with all of the problems going on in the world, many of the problems caused by Hillary Clinton and by Barack Obama.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: All of the problems—the single biggest problem is heroin that pours across our southern border.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s just pouring and destroying their youth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s poisoning the blood of their youth and plenty of other people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have to have strong borders.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have to keep the drugs out of our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We are—right now, we’re getting the drugs, they’re getting the cash.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We need strong borders.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We need absolute—we cannot give amnesty.

transcript_turns.text: Now, I want to build the wall.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We need the wall.

transcript_turns.text: And the Border Patrol, ICE, they all want the wall.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We stop the drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We shore up the border.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: One of my first acts will be to get all of the drug lords, all of the bad ones—we have some bad, bad people in this country that have to go out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to get them out; we’re going to secure the border.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And once the border is secured, at a later date, we’ll make a determination as to the rest.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But we have some bad hombres here, and we’re going to get them out.

transcript_turns.text: Well, as he was talking, I was thinking about a young girl I met here in Las Vegas, Carla, who is very worried that her parents might be deported, because she was born in this country but they were not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They work hard, they do everything they can to give her a good life.

transcript_turns.text: And we would then have to put them on trains, on buses to get them out of our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think that is an idea that is not in keeping with who we are as a nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s an idea that would rip our country apart.

transcript_turns.text: I voted for border security in the United States Senate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And my comprehensive immigration reform plan of course includes border security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I want to put our resources where I think they’re most needed: Getting rid of any violent person.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Anybody who should be deported, we should deport them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: When it comes to the wall that Donald talks about building, he went to Mexico, he had a meeting with the Mexican president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Didn’t even raise it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He choked and then got into a Twitter war because the Mexican president said we’re not paying for that wall.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I think we are both a nation of immigrants and we are a nation of laws and that we can act accordingly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why I’m introducing comprehensive immigration reform within the first 100 days with a path to citizenship.

transcript_turns.text: Chris, I think it’s…

transcript_turns.text: I think I should respond to that.

transcript_turns.text: First of all, I had a very good meeting with the president of Mexico.

transcript_turns.text: Very nice man.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We will be doing very much better with Mexico on trade deals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Believe me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: The NAFTA deal signed by her husband is one of the worst deals ever made of any kind, signed by anybody.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s a disaster.

transcript_turns.text: Hillary Clinton wanted the wall.

transcript_turns.text: Now, she never gets anything done, so naturally the wall wasn’t built.

transcript_turns.text: But Hillary Clinton wanted the wall.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We are a country of laws.

transcript_turns.text: We either have—and by the way…

transcript_turns.text: Well—well, but she said one thing.

transcript_turns.text: I voted for border security, and there are…

transcript_turns.text: Now, what I am also arguing is that bringing undocumented immigrants out from the shadows, putting them into the formal economy will be good, because then employers can’t exploit them and undercut Americans’ wages.

transcript_turns.text: We have millions of people that did it the right way.

transcript_turns.text: They’re on line.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They’re waiting.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to speed up the process, big league, because it’s very inefficient.

transcript_turns.text: But they’re on line and they’re waiting to become citizens.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You would have a disaster on trade, and you will have a disaster with your open borders.

transcript_turns.text: That is…

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton

transcript_turns.text: … to sign immigration reform, and George W.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.text: Well, if you went on to read the rest of the sentence, I was talking about energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You know, we trade more energy with our neighbors than we trade with the rest of the world combined.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I do want us to have an electric grid, an energy system that crosses borders.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think that would be a great benefit to us.

transcript_turns.text: But you are very clearly quoting from WikiLeaks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And what’s really important about WikiLeaks is that the Russian government has engaged in espionage against Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They have hacked American websites, American accounts of private people, of institutions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Then they have given that information to WikiLeaks for the purpose of putting it on the Internet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This has come from the highest levels of the Russian government, clearly, from Putin himself, in an effort, as 17 of our intelligence agencies have confirmed, to influence our election.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I actually think the most important question of this evening, Chris, is, finally, will Donald Trump admit and condemn that the Russians are doing this and make it clear that he will not have the help of Putin in this election, that he rejects Russian espionage against Americans, which he actually encouraged in the past.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Those are the questions we need answered.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve never had anything like this happen in any of our elections before.

transcript_turns.text: That was a great pivot off the fact that she wants open borders, OK?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: How did we get on to Putin?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So just to finish on the borders…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: She wants open borders.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: People are going to pour into our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: People are going to come in from Syria.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: She wants 550 percent more people than Barack Obama, and he has thousands and thousands of people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They have no idea where they come from.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And you see, we are going to stop radical Islamic terrorism in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: She won’t even mention the words, and neither will President Obama.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So I just want to tell you, she wants open borders.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Now we can talk about Putin.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I don’t know Putin.

transcript_turns.text: He said nice things about me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: If we got along well, that would be good.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: If Russia and the United States got along well and went after ISIS, that would be good.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: He has no respect for her.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: He has no respect for our president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I’ll tell you what: We’re in very serious trouble, because we have a country with tremendous numbers of nuclear warheads—1,800, by the way—where they expanded and we didn’t, 1,800 nuclear warheads.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And she’s playing chicken.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Look, Putin…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: … from everything I see, has no respect for this person.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, that’s because he’d rather have a puppet as president of the United States.

transcript_turns.text: No puppet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: No puppet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And it’s pretty clear…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You’re the puppet!

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s pretty clear you won’t admit…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: No, you’re the puppet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: … that the Russians have engaged in cyberattacks against the United States of America, that you encouraged espionage against our people, that you are willing to spout the Putin line, sign up for his wish list, break up NATO, do whatever he wants to do, and that you continue to get help from him, because he has a very clear favorite in this race.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I think that this is such an unprecedented situation.

transcript_turns.text: I am not quoting myself.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: She has no idea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I am quoting 17…

transcript_turns.text: Hillary, you have no idea.

transcript_turns.text: … 17 intelligence—do you doubt 17 military and civilian…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And our country has no idea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: … agencies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Yeah, I doubt it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I doubt it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, he’d rather believe Vladimir Putin than the military and civilian intelligence professionals who are sworn to protect us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I find that just absolutely…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: She doesn’t like Putin because Putin has outsmarted her at every step of the way.

transcript_turns.text: Excuse me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: By Russia or anybody else.

transcript_turns.text: Of course I condemn.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I have no idea.

transcript_turns.text: I never met Putin.

transcript_turns.text: This is not my best friend.

transcript_turns.text: Let me tell you, Putin has outsmarted her and Obama at every single step of the way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Whether it’s Syria, you name it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Missiles.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump

transcript_turns.text: They create warheads, and we can’t.

transcript_turns.text: She has been outsmarted by Putin.

transcript_turns.text: And all you have to do is look at the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They’ve taken over.

transcript_turns.text: We’ve spent $6 trillion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They’ve taken over the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: She has been outsmarted and outplayed worse than anybody I’ve ever seen in any government whatsoever.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And she always will be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I—I find it ironic that he’s raising nuclear weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This is a person who has been very cavalier, even casual about the use of nuclear weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He’s…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: … advocated more countries getting them, Japan, Korea, even Saudi Arabia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He said, well, if we have them, why don’t we use them, which I think is terrifying.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But here’s the deal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The bottom line on nuclear weapons is that when the president gives the order, it must be followed.

transcript_turns.text: There’s about four minutes between the order being given and the people responsible for launching nuclear weapons to do so.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why 10 people who have had that awesome responsibility have come out and, in an unprecedented way, said they would not trust Donald Trump with the nuclear codes or to have his finger on the nuclear button.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I have 200 generals…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: … and admirals, 21 endorsing me, 21 congressional Medal of Honor recipients.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: As far as Japan and other countries, we are being ripped off by everybody in the—we’re defending other countries.

transcript_turns.text: We are spending a fortune doing it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They have the bargain of the century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: All I said is, we have to renegotiate these agreements, because our country cannot afford to defend Saudi Arabia, Japan, Germany, South Korea, and many other places.

transcript_turns.text: We cannot continue to afford—she took that as saying nuclear weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: This is just another lie.

transcript_turns.text: Well, I’m just quoting you when you were asked…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: There’s no quote.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You’re not going to find a quote from me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: … about a potential nuclear—nuclear competition in Asia, you said, you know, go ahead, enjoy yourselves, folks.

transcript_turns.text: That kind…

transcript_turns.text: … of language—well…

transcript_turns.text: And defend yourselves.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I didn’t say nuclear.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And defend yourself.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The United States has kept the peace—the United States has kept the peace through our alliances.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Donald wants to tear up our alliances.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think it makes the world safer and, frankly, it makes the United States safer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I would work with our allies in Asia, in Europe, in the Middle East, and elsewhere.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s the only way we’re going to be able to keep the peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think when the middle class thrives, America thrives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And so my plan is based on growing the economy, giving middle-class families many more opportunities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want us to have the biggest jobs program since World War II, jobs in infrastructure and advanced manufacturing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think we can compete with high-wage countries, and I believe we should.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: New jobs and clean energy, not only to fight climate change, which is a serious problem, but to create new opportunities and new businesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want us to do more to help small business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s where two-thirds of the new jobs are going to come from.

transcript_turns.text: I want us to raise the national minimum wage, because people who live in poverty should not—who work full-time should not still be in poverty.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I sure do want to make sure women get equal pay for the work we do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I feel strongly that we have to have an education system that starts with preschool and goes through college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I want more technical education in high schools and in community colleges, real apprenticeships to prepare young people for the jobs of the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want to make college debt-free and for families making less than $125,000, you will not get a tuition bill from a public college or university if the plan that I worked on with Bernie Sanders is enacted.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we’re going to work hard to make sure that it is, because we are going to go where the money is.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Most of the gains in the last years since the Great Recession have gone to the very top.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So we are going to have the wealthy pay their fair share.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have corporations make a contribution greater than they are now to our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That is a plan that has been analyzed by independent experts which said that it could produce 10 million new jobs.

transcript_turns.text: By contrast, Donald’s plan has been analyzed to conclude it might lose 3.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: 5 million jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Why?

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Because his whole plan is to cut taxes, to give the biggest tax breaks ever to the wealthy and to corporations, adding $20 trillion to our debt, and causing the kind of dislocation that we have seen before, because it truly will be trickle-down economics on steroids.

transcript_turns.text: So the plan I have I think will actually produce greater opportunities.

transcript_turns.text: The plan he has will cost us jobs and possibly lead to another Great Recession.

transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all, before I start on my plan, her plan is going to raise taxes and even double your taxes.

transcript_turns.text: Her tax plan is a disaster.

transcript_turns.text: And she can say all she wants about college tuition.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I’m a big proponent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to do a lot of things for college tuition.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But the rest of the public’s going to be paying for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We will have a massive, massive tax increase under Hillary Clinton’s plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But I’d like to start off where we left, because when I said Japan and Germany, and I’m—not to single them out, but South Korea, these are very rich, powerful countries.

transcript_turns.text: Saudi Arabia, nothing but money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We protect Saudi Arabia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Why aren’t they paying?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: She immediately—when she heard this, I questioned it, and I questioned NATO.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Why aren’t the NATO questioned—why aren’t they paying?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Because they weren’t paying.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Since I did this—this was a year ago—all of a sudden, they’re paying.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve been given a lot—a lot of credit for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: All of a sudden, they’re starting to pay up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They have to pay up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’re protecting people, they have to pay up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I’m a big fan of NATO.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But they have to pay up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: She comes out and said, we love our allies, we think our allies are great.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, it’s awfully hard to get them to pay up when you have somebody saying we think how great they are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have to tell Japan in a very nice way, we have to tell Germany, all of these countries, South Korea, we have to say, you have to help us out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have, during his regime, during President Obama’s regime, we’ve doubled our national debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’re up to $20 trillion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So my plan—we’re going to renegotiate trade deals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have a lot of free trade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have free trade, more free trade than we have right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But we have horrible deals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Our jobs are being taken out by the deal that her husband signed, NAFTA, one of the worst deals ever.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Our jobs are being sucked out of our economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You look at all of the places that I just left, you go to Pennsylvania, you go to Ohio, you go to Florida, you go to any of them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You go upstate New York.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Our jobs have fled to Mexico and other places.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’re bringing our jobs back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I am going to renegotiate NAFTA.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And if I can’t make a great deal—then we’re going to terminate NAFTA and we’re going to create new deals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have trade, but we’re going—we’re going to terminate it, we’re going to make a great trade deal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And if we can’t, we’re going to do it—we’re going to go a separate way, because it has been a disaster.

transcript_turns.text: We are going to cut taxes massively.

transcript_turns.text: They’re going to start hiring people.

transcript_turns.text: We’re going to bring the $2.

transcript_turns.text: 5 trillion…

transcript_turns.text: We are going to start the engine rolling again, because…

transcript_turns.text: Well, he mentioned the debt.

transcript_turns.text: We know how to get control of the debt.

transcript_turns.text: When my husband was president, we went from a $300 billion deficit to a $200 billion surplus and we were actually on the path to eliminating the national debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: When President Obama came into office, he inherited the worst economic disaster since the Great Depression.

transcript_turns.text: He has cut the deficit by two-thirds.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So, yes, one of the ways you go after the debt, one of the ways you create jobs is by investing in people.

transcript_turns.text: So I do have investments, investments in new jobs, investments in education, skill training, and the opportunities for people to get ahead and stay ahead.

transcript_turns.text: That’s the kind of approach that will work.

transcript_turns.text: And let me say that when you inherit the level of economic catastrophe that President Obama inherited, it was a real touch-and-go situation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s a humanitarian nightmare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But it has fallen from the—from any standpoint.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I mean, what do you need, a signed document?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Take a look at Aleppo.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It is so sad when you see what’s happened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And a lot of this is because of Hillary Clinton, because what’s happened is, by fighting Assad, who turned out to be a lot tougher than she thought, and now she’s going to say, oh, he loves Assad, she’s—he’s just much tougher and much smarter than her and Obama.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And everyone thought he was gone two years ago, three years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: He—he aligned with Russia.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: He now also aligned with Iran, who we made very powerful.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We gave them $150 billion back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We give them $1.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: 7 billion in cash.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I mean, cash.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Bundles of cash as big as this stage.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We gave them $1.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: 7 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Now they have—he has aligned with Russia and with Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They don’t want ISIS, but they have other things, because we’re backing—we’re backing rebels.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We don’t know who the rebels are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’re giving them lots of money, lots of everything.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We don’t know who the rebels are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And when and if—and it’s not going to happen, because you have Russia and you have Iran now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But if they ever did overthrow Assad, you might end up with—as bad as Assad is, and he’s a bad guy, but you may very well end up with worse than Assad.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: If she did nothing, we’d be in much better shape.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And this is what’s caused the great migration, where she’s taking in tens of thousands of Syrian refugees, who probably in many cases—not probably, who are definitely…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: … in many cases, ISIS-aligned, and we now have them in our country, and wait until you see—this is going to be the great Trojan horse.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And wait until you see what happens in the coming years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Lots of luck, Hillary.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Thanks a lot for doing a great job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, Chris, first of all, I think a no-fly zone could save lives and could hasten the end of the conflict.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’m well aware of the really legitimate concerns that you have expressed from both the president and the general.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This would not be done just on the first day.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This would take a lot of negotiation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And it would also take making it clear to the Russians and the Syrians that our purpose here was to provide safe zones on the ground.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve had millions of people leave Syria and those millions of people inside Syria who have been dislocated.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I think we could strike a deal and make it very clear to the Russians and the Syrians that this was something that we believe was in the best interests of the people on the ground in Syria, it would help us with our fight against ISIS.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I want to respond to what Donald said about refugees.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He’s made these claims repeatedly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I am not going to let anyone into this country who is not vetted, who we do not have confidence in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I am not going to slam the door on women and children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That picture of that little 4-year-old boy in Aleppo, with the blood coming down his face while he sat in an ambulance, is haunting.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And so we are going to do very careful, thorough vetting.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That does not solve our internal challenges with ISIS and our need to stop radicalization, to work with American Muslim communities who are on the front lines to identify and prevent attacks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: In fact, the killer of the dozens of people at the nightclub in Orlando, the Pulse nightclub, was born in Queens, the same place Donald was born.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So let’s be clear about what the threat is and how we are best going to be able to meet it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And, yes, some of that threat emanates from over in Syria and Iraq, and we’ve got to keep fighting, and I will defeat ISIS, and some of it is we have to up our game and be much smarter here at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But I just have to…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s so ridiculous what she—she will defeat ISIS.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We should have never let ISIS happen in the first place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And right now, they’re in 32 countries.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We should have—wait one second.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They had a cease-fire three weeks ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: A cease-fire, United States, Russia, and Syria.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And during the cease-fire, Russia took over vast swatches of land, and then they said we don’t want the cease-fire anymore.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We are so outplayed on missiles, on cease-fires.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They are outplayed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Now, she wasn’t there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I assume she had nothing to do with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But our country is so outplayed by Putin and Assad, and by the way—and by Iran.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Nobody can believe how stupid our leadership is.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Well, I say they’re wrong, because I’m going to create tremendous jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And we’re bringing GDP from, really, 1 percent, which is what it is now, and if she got in, it will be less than zero.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But we’re bringing it from 1 percent up to 4 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I actually think we can go higher than 4 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I think you can go to 5 percent or 6 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And if we do, you don’t have to bother asking your question, because we have a tremendous machine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We will have created a tremendous economic machine once again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: To do that, we’re taking back jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’re not going to let our companies be raided by other countries where we lose all our jobs, we don’t make our product anymore.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s very sad.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But I’m going to create a—the kind of a country that we were from the standpoint of industry.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We used to be there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’ve given it up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’ve become very, very sloppy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’ve had people that are political hacks making the biggest deals in the world, bigger than companies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You take these big companies, these trade deals are far bigger than these companies, and yet we don’t use our great leaders, many of whom back me and many of whom back Hillary, I must say.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But we don’t use those people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Those are the people—these are the greatest negotiators in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have the greatest businesspeople in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have to use them to negotiate our trade deals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We use political hacks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We use people that get the position because they gave—they made a campaign contribution and they’re dealing with China and people that are very much smarter than they are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: So we have to use our great people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But that being said, we will create an economic machine the likes of which we haven’t seen in many decades.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And people, Chris, will again go back to work and they’ll make a lot of money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And we’ll have companies that will grow and expand and start from new.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, first, when I hear Donald talk like that and know that his slogan is “Make America Great Again,” I wonder when he thought America was great.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And before he rushes and says, “You know, before you and President Obama were there,” I think it’s important to recognize that he has been criticizing our government for decades.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You know, back in 1987, he took out a $100,000 ad in the New York Times, during the time when President Reagan was president, and basically said exactly what he just said now, that we were the laughingstock of the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He was criticizing President Reagan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This is the way Donald thinks about himself, puts himself into, you know, the middle and says, “You know, I alone can fix it,” as he said on the convention stage.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But if you look at the debt, which is the issue you asked about, Chris, I pay for everything I’m proposing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I do not add a penny to the national debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I take that very seriously, because I do think it’s one of the issues we’ve got to come to grips with.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So when I talk about how we’re going to pay for education, how we’re going to invest in infrastructure, how we’re going to get the cost of prescription drugs down, and a lot of the other issues that people talk to me about all the time, I’ve made it very clear we are going where the money is.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We are going to ask the wealthy and corporations to pay their fair share.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And there is no evidence whatsoever that that will slow down or diminish our growth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: In fact, I think just the opposite.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ll have what economists call middle-out growth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to get back to rebuilding the middle class, the families of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s where growth will come from.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I want to invest in you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want to invest in your family.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I think that’s the smartest way to grow the economy, to make the economy fairer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we just have a big disagreement about this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It may be because of our experiences.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You know, he started off with his dad as a millionaire…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Yeah, yeah, we’ve heard—we’ve heard this before, Hillary.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I started off with—my dad was a small-business man.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’ve heard this before.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I think it—you know, it’s a difference that affects how we see the world and what we want to do with the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Hillary.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Could I just respond?

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Because I did disagree with Ronald Reagan very strongly on trade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I disagreed with him.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We should have been much tougher on trade even then.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been waiting for years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Nobody does it right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And frankly, now we’re going to do it right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I’m cutting taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to grow the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s going to grow at a record rate of growth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: No, it’s going to totally help you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And one thing we have to do: Repeal and replace the disaster known as Obamacare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s destroying our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s destroying our businesses, our small business and our big businesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have to repeal and replace Obamacare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You take a look at the kind of numbers that that will cost us in the year ’17, it is a disaster.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: If we don’t repeal and replace—now, it’s probably going to die of its own weight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But Obamacare has to go.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s—the premiums are going up 60 percent, 70 percent, 80 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Next year they’re going to go up over 100 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: And I’m really glad that the premiums have started—at least the people see what’s happening, because she wants to keep Obamacare and she wants to make it even worse, and it can’t get any worse.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Bad health care at the most expensive price.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have to repeal and replace Obamacare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, Chris, I am on record as saying that we need to put more money into the Social Security Trust Fund.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s part of my commitment to raise taxes on the wealthy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: My Social Security payroll contribution will go up, as will Donald’s, assuming he can’t figure out how to get out of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But what we want to do is to replenish the Social Security Trust Fund…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Such a nasty woman.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: … by making sure that we have sufficient resources, and that will come from either raising the cap and/or finding other ways to get more money into it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I will not cut benefits.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want to enhance benefits for low-income workers and for women who have been disadvantaged by the current Social Security system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But what Donald is proposing with these massive tax cuts will result in a $20 trillion additional national debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That will have dire consequences for Social Security and Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I’ll say something about the Affordable Care Act, which he wants to repeal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The Affordable Care Act extended the solvency of the Medicare Trust Fund.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So if he repeals it, our Medicare problem gets worse.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: What we need to do is go after…

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Your husband disagrees with you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: … the long-term health care drivers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to get costs down, increase value, emphasize wellness.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have a plan for doing that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I think that we will be able to get entitlement spending under control by with more resources and smarter decisions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, I would like to say to everyone watching tonight that I’m reaching out to all Americans—Democrats, Republicans, and independents—because we need everybody to help make our country what it should be, to grow the economy, to make it fairer, to make it work for everyone.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need your talents, your skills, your commitments, your energy, your ambition.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You know, I’ve been privileged to see the presidency up close.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I know the awesome responsibility of protecting our country and the incredible opportunity of working to try to make life better for all of you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have made the cause of children and families really my life’s work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s what my mission will be in the presidency.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I will stand up for families against powerful interests, against corporations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I will do everything that I can to make sure that you have good jobs, with rising incomes, that your kids have good educations from preschool through college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Hillary Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I hope you will give me a chance to serve as your president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: She’s raising the money from the people she wants to control.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Doesn’t work that way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: But when I started this campaign, I started it very strongly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It’s called “Make America Great Again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: ” We’re going to make America great.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have a depleted military.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: It has to be helped, has to be fixed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We have the greatest people on Earth in our military.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We don’t take care of our veterans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We take care of illegal immigrants, people that come into the country illegally, better than we take care of our vets.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: That can’t happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Our policemen and women are disrespected.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We need law and order, but we need justice, too.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: Our inner cities are a disaster.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: You get shot walking to the store.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They have no education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: They have no jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: I will do more for African-Americans and Latinos than she can ever do in 10 lifetimes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: All she’s done is talk to the African-Americans and to the Latinos, but they get the vote, and then they come back, they say, we’ll see you in four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We are going to make America strong again, and we are going to make America great again, and it has to start now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Donald Trump
transcript_turns.text: We cannot take four more years of Barack Obama, and that’s what you get when you get her.
